competencies.cefrDescriptor: Can describe an ambition and say what it would mean to them.
Can explain a plan for the next few years and the steps in it.
Can say what they hope will happen and why it matters to them.

competencies.displayName: Describe an ideal job or life
competencies.cefrDescriptor: Can describe the job or life they would like and why.

competencies.displayName: Talk about a goal they gave up
competencies.cefrDescriptor: Can describe something they once wanted and explain what changed.
Can set out the arguments on both sides of a personal decision.
Can explain what drives them, with examples.

competencies.displayName: Talk about worries for the future
competencies.cefrDescriptor: Can describe what concerns them about the future and why.
Can describe a person they admire and explain what they admire about them.
Can say which of several things matters most to them and why.
Can tell a story of several parts and keep the order clear.
Can give the background a listener needs before the main events.
Can identify and describe the moment something changed.
Can bring a story to a close and say how things ended.

competencies.displayName: Say how they felt at the time
competencies.cefrDescriptor: Can describe how they felt during events, not only what happened.
Can report what someone else said or asked.
Can give the gist of something they read, watched or were told.
Can describe an experience that stayed with them and say why.
Can contrast how something was with how it is, over a long period.
Can go back and correct or clarify part of their own account.
Can give a connected account of their experience and training.

competencies.displayName: Explain why they want a role
competencies.cefrDescriptor: Can explain why a position interests them.
Can answer a straightforward question about themselves at length.
Can ask informed questions about a job or course.
Can describe what they are good at and what they find hard, with examples.
Can describe a task or project they were involved in and their part in it.
Can explain why they changed direction and what they learned.
Can discuss hours, pay and conditions in general terms.
Can recommend someone for something and say why.
Can explain a workplace rule or safety requirement and why it exists.
Can report a problem at work and say what should be done.
Can explain a problem that was not anticipated and what they need.
Can ask what can be done and weigh the answers.
Can press a reasonable point politely when a first answer is unsatisfactory.
Can take a complaint further and explain why the response was not enough.
Can propose and agree a practical solution to a problem.
Can explain how a misunderstanding arose and put it right.
Can describe what was damaged or lost, and the circumstances.

competencies.displayName: Ask for something to be put right
competencies.cefrDescriptor: Can ask for a refund, repair or replacement and justify the request.
Can handle a cancellation and make alternative arrangements.
Can apologise for a mistake they made and offer to fix it.
Can say what will happen if something is not resolved.
Can describe what a film or book is about without giving everything away.
Can recommend a film, book or album and justify the recommendation.
Can say what they thought of something and support the judgement.
Can describe a character and what makes them interesting.
Can describe what they generally like and how their taste has changed.
Can compare two films, books or artists and say which they prefer.
Can disagree with someone's opinion of a work and give grounds.
Can describe a concert, show or event they went to.
Can plan an outing with someone, weighing options and times.
Can describe what and how they usually watch, read or listen.
Can describe a recent event and its main points.

competencies.displayName: Give a view on an issue
competencies.cefrDescriptor: Can give an opinion on a familiar issue and support it.

competencies.displayName: Ask what someone makes of it
competencies.cefrDescriptor: Can ask what someone thinks about something in the news.
Can relay something they heard or read, and say where from.
Can question whether something they have been told is true, and give grounds for doubting it.

competencies.displayName: Describe a change in the area
competencies.cefrDescriptor: Can describe something that has changed locally and its effects.
Can describe a custom or celebration and what it involves.
Can compare how something is done in two places.
Can describe a friendship and how it began.
Can describe someone's character at length, with examples.
Can arrange to meet someone they do not know well.
Can pay a compliment and respond to one gracefully.
Can show interest in someone and keep a conversation going.
Can decline an approach politely and without offence.
Can respond to rude or inappropriate behaviour appropriately.
Can talk through a disagreement with someone and repair it.
Can describe what they value in other people.
Can give a friend advice about a personal situation.
Can explain a rule and the reason behind it.
Can say what someone must, should or need not do.
Can ask whether something is permitted and understand the answer.
Can describe the steps of an official or formal procedure.
Can explain that something required was not done, and why.
Can ask for an exception and make a case for it.
Can describe what they are responsible for.
Can understand the main conditions in a straightforward agreement.
Can say what they would do in a hypothetical situation.
Can describe how things would be if a circumstance were different.
Can speculate about why something happened and how sure they are.
Can say what they think will probably happen and why.
Can say that one thing depends on another.
Can express a wish about something they cannot change.
Can talk about a choice they did not make and what might have followed.
Can say what might go wrong and what that would mean.
Can put a case for something over several sentences.
Can respond to an objection with a reason.
Can propose a middle position between two views.
Can accept part of what someone says while keeping their own position.
Can ask someone to think again and give them a reason to.
Can agree to something on a stated condition.
Can refuse firmly without giving offence.
Can restate what has been agreed to confirm it.
Can identify the main point of what someone is saying at length.
Can follow the thread when more than one person is talking.
Can ask a question that follows on from what was just said.
Can invite someone who has not spoken to give their view.

competencies.displayName: Go back to an earlier point
competencies.cefrDescriptor: Can return to something said earlier in the conversation.
Can check one detail without derailing the conversation.
Can show they are following without taking the turn.
Can move the conversation to a related subject.
Can bring a long conversation to a natural close.
Can describe their habits and how healthy they are.
Can give advice about a familiar health matter and explain it.
Can describe a change they made to their habits and its effects.
Can describe a condition they have had for a while and how it affects them.
Can discuss exercise and eating in general terms.
Can describe pressures they are under and how they manage them.
Can ask for a second opinion and explain their concern.
Can follow detailed instructions about treatment or care.
